This script is testing changes to the BBN model for large deer impact risk following the final expert meeting summarising findings phase 2 model validation interviews (06/05/2025)

Changes made:

-   Disturbance (distance to nearest urban/suburban area removed)

-   Calculate focal max DAMS without excluding woodlands as 0 DAMS.

```{r Make-conditional-probability-tables-for-large-deer-BBN}

#THERMOREGULATION INDEX ####---------------------------------------------------------

large_deer_thermoreg <- read.csv("E:/Data_READ_WRITE/R_Scripts_Projects/Amy_Data/Deer impact EW risk maps/large deer/Largedeer_Thermoregulation_Index_Max_Summed_DAMS_1000m_Shelter_Quality_Amy.csv")

data <- subset(large_deer_thermoreg[2:3])

# Define the initial importance weights for each index. These represent the relative
# influence of each factor on deer damage risk.  They will be adjusted conditionally.
importance <- c(MAX_DAMS_1000m = 1, woodland_shelter_value = 0.2)

# Function to assign probability levels
assign_probabilities <- function(row, importance) {
  # Convert categorical factor levels (Low, Medium, High) to numerical scores (1, 2, 3).
  # This allows for weighted calculations.
  scores <- c(
    MAX_DAMS_1000m = as.numeric(factor(row["MAX_DAMS_1000m"], levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"))),
     woodland_shelter_value = as.numeric(factor(row["woodland_shelter_value"], levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")))

  )
  
  # Calculate the total weighted score for the row. This combines the numerical scores
  # with their respective importance weights.
  total_score <- sum(scores * importance)
  
  # Scale the total weighted score to a range of 1-3. This is necessary to map the 
  # score to a meaningful range for the normal distribution.  The min and max scores
  # are calculated based on the possible range given the importance weights.
  min_score <- sum(c(1, 1) * importance)
  max_score <- sum(c(3, 3) * importance)
  scaled_score <- (total_score - min_score) / (max_score - min_score) * 2 + 1 # Scale to 1-3
  print("scaled_score")
  print(scaled_score)

  # Calculate probabilities for each level (Low to High) using a normal distribution.
  # The mean of the distribution is determined by the scaled total score.
  #Higher number of sd = curve becomes flatter - probabilities more evenly distributed.
  #Smaller number of sd = curve becomes steeper - greater difference in probabilities between categories.
  
  print(mean(scaled_score))
  base_probs <- dnorm(1:3, mean = scaled_score, sd = 0.41)
  print(base_probs)
  base_probs <- base_probs / sum(base_probs) # Normalize probabilities to sum to 1.
  print(base_probs)
  
  # Assign names to the probability levels.
  names(base_probs) <- c("Low", "Medium", "High")
  
  # Return the calculated probabilities and the total weighted score.
  return(c(base_probs, total_score = total_score))
}

# Apply the probability assignment function to each row of the data.
probabilities <- t(apply(data, 1, assign_probabilities, importance = importance))

# Combine the original data with the calculated probabilities.
result <- cbind(data, probabilities)

# Print the resulting data frame.
print(result)

# Round numeric values to 3 decimal places for readability.
#result <- result %>% mutate_if(is.numeric, round, digits=3)

# Verify that the probabilities for each row sum to 1.
rowSums(result[, c("Low", "Medium", "High")])

#save cpt

write.csv(result,"E:/Data_READ_WRITE/R_Scripts_Projects/Amy_Data/Deer impact EW risk maps/large deer/Large_Deer_Thermoreg_Index_CPT_post_interviews.csv")

#LARGE DEER ATTRACTION INDEX ####---------------------------------------------------------------------------

large_deer_food <- read.csv("E:/Data_READ_WRITE/R_Scripts_Projects/Amy_Data/Deer impact EW risk maps/large deer/Largedeer_Attraction_Index_Woodland_edge_cover_1000m.Perennial_cover_1000m.Arable_cover_1000m_Amy.csv")

# Select the relevant columns for analysis (Connectivity, Attraction, Thermoregulation).
data <- subset(large_deer_food[2:4])

# Define the initial importance weights for each index. These represent the relative
# influence of each factor on deer damage risk.  They will be adjusted conditionally.
importance <- c(Woodland_edge_cover_1000m = 0.1, Arable_cover_1000m = 1, 
                Perennial_cover_1000m = 1)
# Function to assign probability levels (Low, Low-Medium, Medium, Medium-High, High) 
# to each row based on the weighted combination of input indices.
assign_probabilities <- function(row, importance) {
  # Convert categorical factor levels (Low, Medium, High) to numerical scores (1, 2, 3).
  # This allows for weighted calculations.
  scores <- c(
    Woodland_edge_cover_1000m = as.numeric(factor(row["Woodland_edge_cover_1000m"], levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"))),
    Arable_cover_1000m = as.numeric(factor(row["Arable_cover_1000m"], levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"))),
    Perennial_cover_1000m = as.numeric(factor(row["Perennial_cover_1000m"], levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")))

  )

  #WITHOUT THESE INTERACTIONS, THE ATTRACTION INDEX MAP GOES ALL SPECKLY
    # Conditionally reduce the importance of Perennial cover if Arable cover is High
  #*0.75 means influence of Perennial cover is reduced by 25%
  ## Conditionally increase the importance of Perennial cover cover if Arable cover is Low
  #/0.75 means influence of Perennial cover is increased by 25%
  # if (row["Arable_cover_1000m"] == "Low") {
  #   importance["Arable_cover_1000m"] <- importance["Arable_cover_1000m"] *  0.99
  # } 
  # 
  # else if (row["Perennial_cover_1000m"] == "Low") {
  #   importance["Perennial_cover_1000m"] <- importance["Perennial_cover_1000m"] * 0.99
  # } 
  
  #if perennial cover is low and arable is high, increase importance of arable x 10
  
  if (row["Perennial_cover_1000m"] == "Low" && row["Arable_cover_1000m"] == "High") {
  importance["Arable_cover_1000m"] <- importance["Arable_cover_1000m"] * 10 
}
  
  #if arable is high in general , increase importance of arable x 10
  else if (row["Arable_cover_1000m"] == "High") {
    importance["Arable_cover_1000m"] <- importance["Arable_cover_1000m"] * 10
  } 
  
  #if perennial cover is high, increase importance of perennial x 10
    else if (row["Perennial_cover_1000m"] == "High") {
    importance["Perennial_cover_1000m"] <- importance["Perennial_cover_1000m"] * 10
  } 
  
  #     # Conditionally reduce the importance of edges if Arable cover is High
  # #*0.75 means influence of Perennial cover is reduced by 25%
  # if (row["Arable_cover_1000m"] == "High") {
  #   importance["Woodland_edge_cover_1000m"] <- importance["Woodland_edge_cover_1000m"] * 0.75
  # } 

  importance <- importance / sum(importance) # Normalize after adjustments
  
      # Calculate the total weighted score for the row. This combines the numerical scores
  # with their respective importance weights.
  total_score <- sum(scores * importance)
  
  # Scale the total weighted score to a range of 1-3. This is necessary to map the 
  # score to a meaningful range for the normal distribution.  The min and max scores
  # are calculated based on the possible range given the importance weights.
  min_score <- sum(c(1, 1, 1) * importance) 
  max_score <- sum(c(3, 3, 3) * importance) 
  
  scaled_score <- (total_score - min_score) / (max_score - min_score) * 2 + 1 # Scale to 1-3
  
  # Calculate probabilities for each level (Low to High) using a normal distribution.
  # The mean of the distribution is determined by the scaled total score.
  #Higher number of sd = curve becomes flatter - probabilities more evenly distributed.
  #Smaller number of sd = curve becomes steeper - greater difference in probabilities between categories.
  base_probs <- dnorm(1:3, mean = scaled_score, sd = 0.41)
  base_probs <- base_probs / sum(base_probs) # Normalize probabilities to sum to 1.
  # Assign names to the probability levels.
  names(base_probs) <- c("Low", "Medium", "High")
  
  # Return the calculated probabilities and the total weighted score.
  return(c(base_probs, total_score = total_score))
}

# Apply the probability assignment function to each row of the data.
probabilities <- t(apply(data, 1, assign_probabilities, importance = importance))

# Combine the original data with the calculated probabilities.
result <- cbind(data, probabilities)

# Print the resulting data frame.
print(result, probabilities)

# Round numeric values to 3 decimal places for readability.
#result <- result %>% mutate_if(is.numeric, round, digits=3)

# Verify that the probabilities for each row sum to 1.
rowSums(result[, c("Low", "Medium", "High")])

#save cpt

write.csv(result,"E:/Data_READ_WRITE/R_Scripts_Projects/Amy_Data/Deer impact EW risk maps/large deer/Large_Deer_Attraction_Index_CPT.csv")

#LARGE DEER IMPACT RISK ####----------------------------------------------------------------------
#NO DISTURBANCE METRIC

# Load large deer damage risk data.  This CSV contains the categorical levels 
large_deer_risk <- read.csv("E:/Data_READ_WRITE/R_Scripts_Projects/Amy_Data/Deer impact EW risk maps/large deer/Largedeer_Deer_Damage_Risk.Thermoregulation_Index.Attraction_Index.Woodland_food_value_Index_Amy.csv")

# Select the relevant columns for analysis (Vulnerability, Attraction, Thermoregulation).
data <- subset(large_deer_risk[2:4])
colnames(data)

# Remove rows where Woodland_Food_Value_Index is "Low"
data <- data[data$Woodland_Food_Value_Index != "Low", ]

# Define the initial importance weights for each index. These represent the relative
# influence of each factor on deer damage risk.  They will be adjusted conditionally.
importance <- c(Woodland_Value_Index = 0.3, Attraction_Index = 1, 
                Thermoregulation_Index = 0.2)

# Function to assign probability levels (Low, Low-Medium, Medium, Medium-High, High) 
# to each row based on the weighted combination of input indices.
  # Convert categorical factor levels (Low, Medium, High) to numerical scores (1, 2, 3).
  # This allows for weighted calculations.
  assign_probabilities <- function(row, importance) {
  scores <- c(
    Woodland_Food_Value_Index = as.numeric(factor(row["Woodland_Food_Value_Index"], levels = c("Medium", "High"))),
    Attraction_Index = as.numeric(factor(row["Attraction_Index"], levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"))),
    Thermoregulation_Index = as.numeric(factor(row["Thermoregulation_Index"], levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")))
  )

  # # Conditionally reduce the importance of Attraction_Index if Thermoregulation_Index is High.
  # # This implements the rule that high thermoregulation reduces the influence of attraction (resources outside woods)
  # #* 0.75 means influence of attraction is reduced by 25%
  # if (row["Thermoregulation_Index"] == "High") {
  #   importance["Attraction_Index"] <- importance["Attraction_Index"] * 0.75
  # }
  
  # # Conditionally increase the importance of Attraction_Index if Thermoregulation_Index is Medium or Low.
  # #/ 0.5 means influence of attraction is increased by 50%
  # if (row["Thermoregulation_Index"] %in% c("Low","Medium")) {
  #   importance["Attraction_Index"] <- importance["Attraction_Index"] / 0.50
  # }

  # If Thermoreg is Low, reduce importance to almost 0
  #* 0.99 means influence of thermoregulation is reduced by 99%
  if (row["Thermoregulation_Index"] %in% c("Low")) {
    importance["Thermoregulation_Index"] <- importance["Thermoregulation_Index"] * 0.99
  }
  
  # If Attraction_Index is high, increase importance by 80%
  if (row["Attraction_Index"] %in% c("High")) {
    importance["Attraction_Index"] <- importance["Attraction_Index"] / 0.8
  }
  
  # Re-normalize importance weights so they sum to 1 after adjustment.
  importance <- importance / sum(importance)
  
  # Calculate the total weighted score for the row. This combines the numerical scores
  # with their respective importance weights.
  total_score <- sum(scores * importance)
  
  # # Scale the total weighted score to a range of 1-5. This is necessary to map the 
  # # score to a meaningful range for the normal distribution.  The min and max scores
  # # are calculated based on the possible range given the importance weights.
  # min_score <- sum(c(2, 1, 1) * importance)
  # max_score <- sum(c(3, 3, 3) * importance)
  
  # Define actual numerical range per index
min_values <- c(Woodland_Food_Value_Index = 1, Attraction_Index = 1, Thermoregulation_Index = 1)
max_values <- c(Woodland_Food_Value_Index = 2, Attraction_Index = 3, Thermoregulation_Index = 3)

min_score <- sum(min_values * importance)
max_score <- sum(max_values * importance)
  
  scaled_score <- (total_score - min_score) / (max_score - min_score) * 4 + 1 # Scale to 1-5
  
  # Calculate probabilities for each level (Low to High) using a normal distribution.
  # The mean of the distribution is determined by the scaled total score.
  #Higher number of sd = curve becomes flatter - probabilities more evenly distributed.
  #Smaller number of sd = curve becomes steeper - greater difference in probabilities between categories.
  base_probs <- dnorm(1:5, mean = scaled_score, sd = 0.41)
  base_probs <- base_probs / sum(base_probs) # Normalize probabilities to sum to 1.
  
  # Assign names to the probability levels.
  names(base_probs) <- c("Low", "Low_Medium", "Medium", "Medium_High", "High")
  
  # Return the calculated probabilities and the total weighted score.
  return(c(base_probs, total_score = total_score))
}

# Apply the probability assignment function to each row of the data.
probabilities <- t(apply(data, 1, assign_probabilities, importance = importance))

str(probabilities)

# Combine the original data with the calculated probabilities.
result <- cbind(data, probabilities)

# Print the resulting data frame.
print(result)

# Round numeric values to 3 decimal places for readability.
#result <- result %>% mutate_if(is.numeric, round, digits=3)

# Verify that the probabilities for each row sum to 1.
rowSums(result[, c("Low", "Low_Medium", "Medium", "Medium_High", "High")])

#save cpt

write.csv(result,"E:/Data_READ_WRITE/R_Scripts_Projects/Amy_Data/Deer impact EW risk maps/large deer/Large_Deer_Damage_Risk_CPT_post_interviews.csv")
```

```{r Woodland-edge-raster}
# Create the IFT_ID column based on the IFT_IOA values
#1 = open woodland types
#2 = mature woodland types
#3 = non woodland habitats with potential for foraging

nfi <- nfi %>%
  mutate(group_ID = case_when(
    IFT_IOA %in% c("Assumed woodland","Failed","Windblow","Ground prep","Felled","Low density", "Young trees","Shrub") ~ 1,
    IFT_IOA %in% c("Conifer","Broadleaved","Mixed mainly broadleaved","Mixed mainly conifer","Coppice with standards","Coppice") ~ 2,
    #IFT_IOA %in% c("Agricultural land","Grassland","Other vegetation") ~ 3, #don't need this line- boundaries function automatically obtains edges of classes (1 and 2) with NAs
    TRUE ~ NA_real_  # This handles other values (if needed, or you can leave it out)
  ))

nfi_rast <- fasterize::fasterize(nfi, template_rast, field = "group_ID")

# Get boundaries between 1 and 2
 boundaries_nfi <- boundaries(nfi_rast, type = "inner", classes = TRUE, #make edges between classes as well as NA
                              directions = 8, #search for edges in 8 directions
                              asNA = TRUE) #non-edges returned as NA
```

```{r MAX-DAMS-WITHIN-1000m}
#DAMS_open_raster_test <- crop(DAMS_open_raster, tiles)

circle.buff = raster::focalWeight(dams_crop, d=1000, type="circle",fillNA=T )#Create buffer
circle.buff[circle.buff > 0] <- 1   # replacing weights by 1
Focal1000_DAMS= raster::focal(x=dams_crop, w=circle.buff, fun=sum, na.rm=T, pad=TRUE, padValue=NA#,

beepr::beep()

#Aggregate to patch, where the score for each patch is the normalised maximum summed DAMS score for any pixel in patch
# Assuming you have a patch identifier, e.g., 'patch_id' in your woodland polygons
patch_agg <- raster::extract(Focal1000_DAMS, unmerged_woods, fun=max, na.rm=TRUE, df=TRUE)

patch_agg$poly_id <- 1:nrow(patch_agg)

patch_agg <- patch_agg %>% rename(#group_ID = poly_id,
                                  max_dams_1000_non_wood_2023 = layer)

#left_join the max summed DAMS score to GB_polys_merged

polys_unmerged_max_summed_DAMS <- left_join(unmerged_woods, patch_agg, by=c("poly_id"="poly_id"))

polys_unmerged_max_summed_DAMS <- st_as_sf(polys_unmerged_max_summed_DAMS)

#Rasterize

raster = template_rast_crop,
field = "max_dams_1000_non_wood_2023")
```

```{r Reclassify-continuous-into-categorical-variables}

df_cat <- df.no.nas.full 

df_cat <- df_cat %>% rename(Woodland_food_value = woodland_food_value_raster,
                            Woodland_shelter_value = woodland_shelter_value_raster)

#Edges within 1000m
#LOW/MED/HIGH
df_cat$Focal1000_EDGES_PERC<- ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_EDGES_PERC <= 5, "Low",
          ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_EDGES_PERC > 5 & df_cat$Focal1000_EDGES_PERC <=20, "Medium",
          ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_EDGES_PERC>20, "High", NA)))#)

# Woodland forage quality
df_cat$Woodland_food_value <-
         ifelse(df_cat$Woodland_food_value==1, "Medium",
            ifelse(df_cat$Woodland_food_value==2, "High", NA))

# Woodland shelter quality
df_cat$Woodland_shelter_value <-
            ifelse(df_cat$Woodland_shelter_value==1, "Low",
            ifelse(df_cat$Woodland_shelter_value==2, "Medium",
            ifelse(df_cat$Woodland_shelter_value==3 , "High", NA)))


#Arable within 1000m
#LOW/MED/HIGH
#Manually adjusted
df_cat$Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC <- ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC <=0, "Low",
           ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC > 0 & df_cat$Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC <=50, "Medium",
           ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC >50, "High", NA)))

#Perennial cover within 1000m
df_cat$Focal1000_PEREN_PERC <- ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_PEREN_PERC <=25, "Low",
          ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_PEREN_PERC > 25 & df_cat$Focal1000_PEREN_PERC <=50, "Medium",
          ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_PEREN_PERC >50, "High", NA)))#)

#Max summed DAMS within 1000m
df_cat$Focal1000_MAX_DAMS <- ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_MAX_DAMS <= 0.60, "Low",
                      ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_MAX_DAMS > 0.60  & df_cat$Focal1000_MAX_DAMS <=0.80, "Medium",
                      ifelse(df_cat$Focal1000_MAX_DAMS > 0.80, "High", NA)))#)


#ensure factor levels in correct order 
df_cat$Focal1000_MAX_DAMS <- factor(df_cat$Focal1000_MAX_DAMS, levels = c("Low","Medium","High"))

df_cat$Woodland_food_value<- factor(df_cat$Woodland_food_value, levels= c("Medium","High"))

df_cat$Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC <- factor(df_cat$Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC, levels = c("Low","Medium","High"))

df_cat$Focal1000_EDGES_PERC<- factor(df_cat$Focal1000_EDGES_PERC, levels = c("Low","Medium","High"))

df_cat$Focal1000_PEREN_PERC <- factor(df_cat$Focal1000_PEREN_PERC, levels = c("Low","Medium","High"))

df_cat$Woodland_shelter_value <- factor(df_cat$Woodland_shelter_value, levels = c("Low","Medium","High"))

#unique(df_cat$NEAREST_URB_SUBURB)
unique(df_cat$Focal1000_MAX_DAMS)
unique(df_cat$Focal1000_PEREN_PERC)
unique(df_cat$Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC)
unique(df_cat$Focal1000_EDGES_PERC)
unique(df_cat$Woodland_food_value)
unique(df_cat$Woodland_shelter_value)
```

```{r CPT-for-Attraction-index}
# Define the dimensions
attraction_index_levels <- c("Low", "Medium", "High")
peren_area_levels <- unique(attraction_cpt_df$Perennial_cover_1000m)
arable_area_levels <- unique(attraction_cpt_df$Arable_cover_1000m)
edge_levels <- unique(attraction_cpt_df$Woodland_edge_cover_1000m)

# Initialize the array with dimensions and names
attraction_index_cpt <- array(
  NA,  # Placeholder value
  dim = c(length(attraction_index_levels),
          length(peren_area_levels),
          length(edge_levels),
          length(arable_area_levels)),
  dimnames = list(
    attraction_index = attraction_index_levels,
    Focal1000_PEREN_PERC = peren_area_levels,
    Focal1000_EDGES_PERC = edge_levels,
    Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC = arable_area_levels
  )
)

# Populate the array
for (i in 1:nrow(attraction_cpt_df)) {
  peren_val <- attraction_cpt_df$Perennial_cover_1000m[i]
  edge_val <- attraction_cpt_df$Woodland_edge_cover_1000m[i]
  arable_val <- attraction_cpt_df$Arable_cover_1000m[i]

  attraction_index_cpt["Low", as.character(peren_val), as.character(edge_val), as.character(arable_val)] <- attraction_cpt_df$Low[i]
  attraction_index_cpt["Medium", as.character(peren_val), as.character(edge_val), as.character(arable_val)] <- attraction_cpt_df$Medium[i]
  attraction_index_cpt["High", as.character(peren_val), as.character(edge_val), as.character(arable_val)] <- attraction_cpt_df$High[i]

}
```

```{r Create-BBN-structure}

# Step 1: Explicitly define the nodes in the network
nodes <- c(
  "Woodland_food_value",
  "Woodland_shelter_value",
  #"dist_to_urban",
  "Focal1000_PEREN_PERC",
  "Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC",
  "MAX_DAMS_1000m",
  "Focal1000_EDGES_PERC",
  "attraction_index",
  "thermoreg_index",
  "wood_value_index",
  #"urban_dist_index",
  "large_risk_index"
)

#empty graph
library(bnlearn)
e = empty.graph(nodes)

arc.set = matrix(c("Woodland_food_value", "wood_value_index",
                   "Focal1000_PEREN_PERC", "attraction_index",
                   "Focal1000_EDGES_PERC", "attraction_index",
                   "Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC", "attraction_index",
                   "MAX_DAMS_1000m","thermoreg_index",
                   "Woodland_shelter_value","thermoreg_index",
                   "thermoreg_index","large_risk_index",
                   "wood_value_index","large_risk_index",
                   "attraction_index","large_risk_index"),
                 ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE,
                 dimnames = list(NULL, c("from", "to")))

arcs(e) <- arc.set

model_string <- modelstring(e) 

net<-model2network(model_string) 
# You dont need to repeat the names of the nodes with parents (child nodes) 

# Custom fitting network (matching up the nodes to their CPTs)
dfit = custom.fit(net, dist = list(Woodland_food_value = wood_food_value_cpt, 
                                   Focal1000_PEREN_PERC = peren_cpt,
                                   Focal1000_EDGES_PERC = edge_cpt,
                                   MAX_DAMS_1000m = dams_cpt,
                                   Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC = arable_cpt,
                                   Woodland_shelter_value = wood_shelter_value_cpt,
                                   thermoreg_index = thermoreg_index_cpt,
                                   attraction_index =attraction_index_cpt,
                                   large_risk_index=large_risk_index_cpt,
                                   wood_value_index=wood_value_index_cpt))

#Plot BN structure ####
#graphviz.plot(net)

#Check parameters ####
dfit
```

```{r BBN-predictions}
predict_dat <- df_cat %>%st_drop_geometry() #%>% #drop geometry
  #mutate(across(where(is.character), toupper)) %>% #convert characters to upper case
  #dplyr::select(-c("x","y"))

#Ensure variable names match those in BBN
predict_dat<-predict_dat%>%rename(
  Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC=Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC,
  Focal1000_PEREN_PERC=Focal1000_PEREN_PERC,
  MAX_DAMS_1000m=Focal1000_MAX_DAMS,
  Woodland_food_value=Woodland_food_value,
  Focal1000_EDGES_PERC = Focal1000_EDGES_PERC)

#Make empty columns for the latent (unobserved) variables

predict_dat$attraction_index <- NA
predict_dat$wood_value_index <- NA
predict_dat$thermoreg_index <- NA
predict_dat$large_risk <- NA

head(predict_dat)

#Ensure all columns are factors, not characters
predict_dat <- predict_dat %>% mutate_all(as.factor)

#Ensure factor levels are in correct order
levels(predict_dat$Woodland_food_value)<-c("Medium", "High")
levels(predict_dat$Focal1000_PEREN_PERC)<-c("Low", "Medium", "High")
levels(predict_dat$Focal1000_ARABLE_PERC)<-c("Low", "Medium", "High")
levels(predict_dat$MAX_DAMS_1000m)<-c("Low", "Medium", "High")
levels(predict_dat$Focal1000_EDGES_PERC)<-c("Low", "Medium", "High")
levels(predict_dat$Woodland_shelter_value) <- c("Low", "Medium", "High")

predict_dat$attraction_index <- factor(NA, levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"))
predict_dat$wood_value_index <- factor(NA, levels = c("Medium", "High"))
predict_dat$thermoreg_index <- factor(NA, levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"))
predict_dat$large_risk <- factor(NA, levels = c("Low", "Low_Medium", "Medium", "Medium_High", "High"))


all_nodes <- names(dfit)

#PREDICTIONS TAKE A LONG TIME, ABOUT 3 MINUTES PER LINE
#Predict values for latent variables
pred_thermoreg = predict(object=dfit,node="thermoreg_index",data=predict_dat, method = "parents")
pred_fpi = predict(dfit,node="attraction_index",data=predict_dat, method = "parents")
pred_wood_value = predict(dfit,node="wood_value_index",data=predict_dat, method = "parents")

#fill the columns
predict_dat$thermoreg_index <- pred_thermoreg
predict_dat$attraction_index <- pred_fpi
predict_dat$wood_value_index <- pred_wood_value

#Predict damage
pred_damage = predict(dfit,node = "large_risk_index",data = predict_dat,method = "parents")
predict_dat$large_risk <- pred_damage

# # scatter plot of forage pressure index and alt forage quality
# predict_dat_sample <- predict_dat[sample(nrow(predict_dat), 10000), ]
# ggplot(predict_dat_sample, aes(x = alt_forage_qual_1000m, y = attraction_index)) +
#   geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0.2, size = 3, color = "blue") +
#   labs(x = "Alt forage Q", y = "Index") +
#   theme_minimal()

#Add damage risk back into spatial dataset

df_cat$pred_damage <- pred_damage
df_cat$pred_thermoreg <- pred_thermoreg
df_cat$pred_attraction_index <- pred_fpi
df_cat$pred_wood_value_index <- pred_wood_value

beepr::beep()
```
